newsitem.title: USA: Bowles sees fast-track trade announcement soon.
newsitem.headline: Bowles sees fast-track trade announcement soon.

text.p: White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles said on Thursday the Clinton administration was confident of getting fast-track trade authority and there could be an announcement on the issue "shortly".

Bowles told reporters he and others in the Clinton administration were meeting on Thursday and Friday with Congressional leaders, adding, "hopefully we will agree on timing; so I would hope you would see an announcement shortly."

Fast-track trade authority would allow the administration to negotiate trade agreements without the fear that Congress might later change them. Clinton wants fast-track trade authority from Congress in order to negotiate an expansion of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) to include Chile, as well as other deals.
The administration has yet to send Congress proposed legislation, saying it is trying to work out a bill that would win bipartisan support.

Bowles said he and U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky had met and would continue to meet with members of Congress on this issue. "We want to attract the broadest possible support," Bowles said. "We believe that we will be able to get fast-track authority, we believe it will be a significant battle," Bowles said. "It is something that we're committed to."

On another trade matter, Bowles said getting congressional approval for President Bill Clinton's decison to renew China's Most Favored Nation trading status "will be difficult, but we believe it is do-able."
